# Objects

## Creating and naming objects

`name <- value`: **`<-`** creates objects

```{r, echo=TRUE}
age <- 25
```

::: fragment
```{r, echo=TRUE}
age <- age + 1          # overwrite
```
:::

::: fragment
```{r, echo=TRUE}
age_months <- age * 12  # use it to create a new object
```
:::

::: fragment
```{r, echo=TRUE}
age_months
```
:::

::: incremental
-   names **start with a letter**, no spaces: `my_data`, `x1` (not `1x`, `my data`)
-   R is **case-sensitive**: `Name` and `name` are two different objects
-   `rm(x)` removes one object, `rm(list = ls())` removes all
:::

## Data types

```{r, echo=TRUE}
class(3.14)      # numeric
```

::: fragment
```{r, echo=TRUE}
class(5L)        # integer
```
:::

::: fragment
```{r, echo=TRUE}
class("hello")   # character: always in quotes
```
:::

::: fragment
```{r, echo=TRUE}
class(TRUE)      # logical
```
:::

::: fragment
```{r, echo=TRUE}
class("5")       # in quotes: character
```
:::

# Operators

## Mathematical operators and functions

| operator        | meaning                   | example     | result |
|-----------------|---------------------------|-------------|--------|
| `+` `-` `*` `/` | arithmetic                | `6 * 2 / 4` | `3`    |
| `^`             | power                     | `2 ^ 3`     | `8`    |
| `%%`            | remainder of the division | `9 %% 2`    | `1`    |

```{r, echo=TRUE}
(1 + 2) * 3                  # parentheses first
```

::: fragment
```{r, echo=TRUE}
sqrt(16); abs(-7); round(3.14159, 2)
```
:::

## Relational and logical operators

```{r, echo=TRUE}
x <- 30
```

::: fragment
```{r, echo=TRUE}
x == 30; x != 30; x >= 18     # compare: TRUE or FALSE
```
:::

::: fragment
```{r, echo=TRUE}
x %in% c(10, 20, 30)          # is x one of these values?
```
:::

::: fragment
```{r, echo=TRUE}
x > 25 & x < 60               # AND: both TRUE
```
:::

::: fragment
```{r, echo=TRUE}
x < 18 | x > 60               # OR: at least one TRUE
```
:::

::: fragment
```{r, echo=TRUE}
!(x > 25)                     # NOT
```
:::

## TRUE and FALSE are numbers

`TRUE` counts as **1**, `FALSE` as **0**: `sum()` counts, `mean()` gives the proportion

```{r, echo=TRUE}
scores <- c(18, 25, 30, 22, 27)
```

::: fragment
```{r, echo=TRUE}
scores >= 25
```
:::

::: fragment
```{r, echo=TRUE}
sum(scores >= 25)       # how many?
```
:::

::: fragment
```{r, echo=TRUE}
mean(scores >= 25)      # which proportion?
```
:::

# Vectors

## Creating vectors

One dimension, **all elements of the same type**

```{r, echo=TRUE}
num1 <- c(4, 8, 15); num1
```

::: fragment
```{r, echo=TRUE}
num2 <- 1:5; num2
```
:::

::: fragment
```{r, echo=TRUE}
num3 <- seq(from = 0, to = 10, by = 2); num3
```
:::

::: fragment
```{r, echo=TRUE}
ch1 <- rep(c("x", "y"), times = 2); ch1   # whole vector
```
:::

::: fragment
```{r, echo=TRUE}
ch2 <- rep(c("x", "y"), each = 2); ch2    # each element
```
:::

::: fragment
```{r, echo=TRUE}
ch3 <- rep(c("x", "y"), each = 2, times = 2); ch3
```
:::

## Types: `is.` and `as.`

Mixing types converts everything to **one type**:

```{r, echo=TRUE}
c(1, 2, "three")                     # all character
```

::: fragment
```{r, echo=TRUE}
c(1, 2, NA, 4)                       # NA keeps the type
```
:::

::::: fragment
`is.` tests the type, `as.` converts it:

```{r, echo=TRUE, warning=TRUE}
is.numeric(c(1, 0, 3))
```

::: fragment
```{r, echo=TRUE, warning=TRUE}
as.logical(c(1, 0, 3))               # 0 is FALSE, others TRUE
```
:::

::: fragment
```{r, echo=TRUE, warning=TRUE}
as.numeric(c("1", "2", "three"))     # cannot convert: NA
```
:::
:::::

## Operations and missing values

Operations work **element by element**, summary functions return **one value**

```{r, echo=TRUE}
temps <- c(12, 18, NA, 31, 7)
```

::: fragment
```{r, echo=TRUE}
temps * 2
```
:::

::: fragment
```{r, echo=TRUE}
mean(temps)                  # one NA makes the result NA
```
:::

::: fragment
```{r, echo=TRUE}
mean(temps, na.rm = TRUE)    # remove the NAs first
```
:::

::: fragment
```{r, echo=TRUE}
is.na(temps)
```
:::

::: fragment
```{r, echo=TRUE}
sum(is.na(temps))            # how many NAs?
```
:::

## Indexing by position

```{r, echo=TRUE}
temps <- c(12, 18, 25, 31, 7)
```

::: fragment
```{r, echo=TRUE}
temps[2]                  # the second element
```
:::

::: fragment
```{r, echo=TRUE}
temps[c(1, 3)]            # the first and the third
```
:::

::: fragment
```{r, echo=TRUE}
temps[2:4]                # from the second to the fourth
```
:::

::: fragment
```{r, echo=TRUE}
temps[length(temps)]      # the last one
```
:::

::: fragment
```{r, echo=TRUE}
temps[-1]                 # all except the first
```
:::

## Indexing: logical conditions and `which()`

```{r, echo=TRUE}
temps
temps > 20                        # the condition
```

::: fragment
```{r, echo=TRUE}
temps[temps > 20]                 # keep where TRUE
```
:::

::: fragment
```{r, echo=TRUE}
temps[temps > 10 & temps < 30]
```
:::

::: fragment
```{r, echo=TRUE}
which(temps > 20)                 # the positions
```
:::

## Modifying with indexing

Indexing + `<-` **modifies** only the selected elements:

```{r, echo=TRUE}
scores <- c(18, NA, 30, 22, NA)
```

::: fragment
```{r, echo=TRUE}
scores[1] <- 20                   # by position
```
:::

::: fragment
```{r, echo=TRUE}
scores[is.na(scores)] <- 0        # by condition
```
:::

::: fragment
```{r, echo=TRUE}
scores[scores < 21] <- 21
```
:::

::: fragment
```{r, echo=TRUE}
scores
```
:::

# Factors

## Factors: codes + levels

```{r, echo=TRUE}
group <- factor(x = c("placebo", "caffeine", "nicotine",
                  "placebo", "caffeine"))
```

::: fragment
```{r, echo=TRUE}
group
```
:::

::: fragment
```{r, echo=TRUE}
levels(group)
```
:::

::: fragment
```{r, echo=TRUE}
as.integer(group)  # caffeine=1, nicotine=2, placebo=3
```
:::

::: fragment
```{r, echo=TRUE}
table(group)
```
:::

## Levels stay, even when unused

```{r, echo=TRUE}
no_placebo <- group[group != "placebo"]
no_placebo # "placebo" is still a level
```

::: fragment
```{r, echo=TRUE}
no_placebo <- droplevels(no_placebo)
```
:::

::: fragment
```{r, echo=TRUE}
levels(no_placebo)
```
:::

## Adding a new level

To use a **new** value, first add it to the levels

```{r, echo=TRUE}
group
levels(group) <- c(levels(group), "water")
```

::: fragment
```{r, echo=TRUE}
group[1] <- "water"
group
```
:::

## Reorder vs rename

```{r, echo=TRUE}
group <- factor(x = c("placebo", "caffeine", "nicotine",
                  "placebo", "caffeine"))
```

::: fragment
```{r, echo=TRUE}
# REORDER: placebo first (reference category), same data
group_ord <- factor( x = c("placebo", "caffeine", "nicotine",
                  "placebo", "caffeine"),
  levels = c("placebo", "caffeine", "nicotine"))
```
:::

::: fragment
```{r, echo=TRUE}
levels(group_ord)
```
:::

:::: fragment
```{r, echo=TRUE}
# RENAME: by position, check levels() first!
levels(group_ord) <- c("PLA", "CAF", "NIC")
```

::: fragment
```{r, echo=TRUE}
group_ord
```
:::
::::

## Reorder and rename in one step

`factor()` with both arguments:

-   **`levels`**: the existing values, in the order we want
-   **`labels`**: their new names, in the same order

```{r, echo=TRUE}
group_new <- factor(x = c("placebo", "caffeine", "nicotine",
                  "placebo", "caffeine"),
  levels = c("placebo", "caffeine", "nicotine"),
  labels = c("PLA", "CAF", "NIC"))
```

::: fragment
```{r, echo=TRUE}
group_new
```
:::

::: fragment
```{r, echo=TRUE}
levels(group_new)
```
:::

## Ordered factors and numbers

For **ordinal** categories (`<` and `>` make sense), set the order **and** `ordered = TRUE`

```{r, echo=TRUE}
freq <- factor(x = c("often", "never", "sometimes"),
  levels = c("never", "sometimes", "often"), ordered = TRUE)
```

::: fragment
```{r, echo=TRUE}
freq > "never"
```
:::

:::: fragment
To get back numbers saved as a factor: first to text, then to numbers

```{r, echo=TRUE}
points_f <- factor(c(10, 30, 10, 20))
```

::: fragment
```{r, echo=TRUE}
as.numeric(as.character(points_f))
```
:::
::::

# Lists

## Lists: different types and sizes

```{r, echo=TRUE}
participant <- list(name = "Anna",
                    rts = c(450, 520, 380),
                    passed = TRUE,
                    other = list(mom_age = c(27, 34, 40, 18),
                                 degree = c("bachelor")
                    ))
```

::: fragment
```{r, echo=TRUE}
str(participant)
```
:::

## Looking at a list

```{r, echo=TRUE}
length(participant)
```

::: fragment
```{r, echo=TRUE}
names(participant)
```
:::

## `[ ]`, `[[ ]]` and `$`

```{r, echo=TRUE}
participant[2]          # [ ]: a smaller LIST
```

::: fragment
```{r, echo=TRUE}
participant[[2]]        # [[ ]]: the element itself
```
:::

::: fragment
```{r, echo=TRUE}
participant$rts         # $: the element, by name
```
:::

::: fragment
```{r, echo=TRUE}
participant$rts[3]      # then index inside it
```
:::

::: fragment
```{r, echo=TRUE}
class(participant[2]); class(participant[[2]])
```
:::

## Modifying lists

```{r, echo=TRUE}
participant$age <- 24              # add an element
```

::: fragment
```{r, echo=TRUE}
participant$passed <- FALSE        # change an element
```
:::

::: fragment
```{r, echo=TRUE}
participant$rts[1] <- 455          # change inside an element
```
:::

::: fragment
```{r, echo=TRUE}
str(participant)
```
:::

# Matrices and arrays

## Matrices: two dimensions, one type

```{r, echo=TRUE}
m <- matrix(data = 1:6, nrow = 2, ncol = 3)   # by column
```

::: fragment
```{r, echo=TRUE}
m
```
:::

::: fragment
```{r, echo=TRUE}
# by row
matrix(data = 1:6, nrow = 2, ncol = 3, byrow = TRUE)
```
:::

::: fragment
```{r, echo=TRUE}
dim(m); nrow(m); ncol(m)
```
:::

## Indexing matrices: `[row, column]`

```{r, echo=TRUE}
m[2, 3]          # one element
```

::: fragment
```{r, echo=TRUE}
m[1, ]           # the whole first row
```
:::

::: fragment
```{r, echo=TRUE}
m[, 2]           # the whole second column
```
:::

::: fragment
```{r, echo=TRUE}
m[m > 3]         # logical condition
```
:::

:::: fragment
```{r, echo=TRUE}
m[m > 3] <- 0    # modify
```

::: fragment
```{r, echo=TRUE}
m
```
:::
::::

## Joining matrices and vectors

```{r, echo=TRUE}
a <- 1:3
```

::: fragment
```{r, echo=TRUE}
b <- c(10, 20, 30)
```
:::

::::::: columns
:::: {.column width="50%"}
::: fragment
```{r, echo=TRUE}
cbind(a, b)   # as columns
```
:::
::::

:::: {.column width="50%"}
::: fragment
```{r, echo=TRUE}
rbind(a, b)   # as rows
```
:::
::::
:::::::

::: fragment
Still **one type only**: adding text turns everything into text

```{r, echo=TRUE}
cbind(a, c("x", "y", "z"))
```
:::

# Dataframes

## Dataframes: columns of different types

Each column is a **vector** (all the same length): a list with a rectangular shape

```{r, echo=TRUE}
df <- data.frame(id = c("P1", "P2", "P3", "P4", "P5"),
                 group = c("ctrl", "trt", "ctrl", "trt", "trt"),
                 age = c(22, 27, 31, NA, 24),
                 score = c(18, 25, 30, 22, 27))
```

::: fragment
```{r, echo=TRUE}
df
```
:::

## Looking at a dataframe

```{r, echo=TRUE}
str(df)
```

::: fragment
```{r, echo=TRUE}
dim(df); names(df)
```
:::

::: fragment
```{r, echo=TRUE}
head(df, n = 2)
```
:::

::: fragment
`summary(df)` and `table(df$group)` are also useful checks
:::

## Extracting a column as a vector

```{r, echo=TRUE}
df$age               # a column: a vector
```

::: fragment
```{r, echo=TRUE}
df[["age"]]          # the same
```
:::

## Extracting a column as a dataframe

```{r, echo=TRUE}
df["age"]            # a dataframe with one column
```

::: fragment
```{r, echo=TRUE}
df[3]                # the same, by position
```
:::

## Extracting rows

`df[rows, columns]`: leave a position **empty** to keep everything

```{r, echo=TRUE}
df
```

::: fragment
```{r, echo=TRUE}
df[2, ]              # the second row
```
:::

## Extracting cells

```{r, echo=TRUE}
df[2, "score"]       # one cell: row 2, column score
```

::: fragment
```{r, echo=TRUE}
df[1:2, c("id", "score")]
```
:::

## Selecting rows with conditions

`df[rows, columns]`: the condition goes in the **rows** position

```{r, echo=TRUE}
df
```

::: fragment
```{r, echo=TRUE}
df[df$score > 20, ]
```
:::

## Combining conditions

```{r, echo=TRUE}
df[df$group == "trt" & df$score > 22, c("id", "score")]
```

## Selecting rows with `subset()`

Same result, without repeating `df$`:

```{r, echo=TRUE}
subset(df, subset = group == "trt" & score > 22,
       select = c(id, score))
```

## Creating a new column

`df$new_column <- value`: one value for each row

```{r, echo=TRUE}
df$passed <- df$score >= 25
df
```

## A new column from another column

```{r, echo=TRUE}
df$score_100 <- df$score / 30 * 100
df
```

## Creating a column with `ifelse()`

A new column that depends on a **condition**

```{r, echo=TRUE}
df$level <- ifelse(df$score >= 25, "high", "low")
df
```

## Changing the type of a column

```{r, echo=TRUE}
df$group <- as.factor(df$group)
str(df)
```

## Changing one cell

Select the cell with a condition, then assign the new value

```{r, echo=TRUE}
df$age[df$id == "P4"] <- 29
df
```

## Removing a column

Assign **`NULL`** to the column

```{r, echo=TRUE}
df$score_100 <- NULL
df
```

## Counting

```{r, echo=TRUE}
table(df$group)                     # frequencies
```

::: fragment
```{r, echo=TRUE}
table(df$group, df$level)           # contingency table
```
:::

## Sorting rows: `order()`

`order()` gives the **positions** of the rows, from the lowest to the highest value

```{r, echo=TRUE}
df$score
order(df$score)
```

::: fragment
We use these positions to select the rows: the rows are now **sorted** by score

```{r, echo=TRUE}
df_sorted <- df[order(df$score), ]
df_sorted
```
:::

## Sorting from the highest

`decreasing = TRUE`

```{r, echo=TRUE}
df_sorted <- df[order(df$score, decreasing = TRUE), ]
df_sorted
```

## Missing values in a dataframe

```{r, echo=TRUE}
df$age[2] <- NA
```

::: fragment
```{r, echo=TRUE}
df$age
```
:::

::: fragment
```{r, echo=TRUE}
sum(is.na(df$age))                  # how many NAs?
```
:::

::: fragment
```{r, echo=TRUE}
mean(df$age, na.rm = TRUE)
```
:::

::: fragment
```{r, echo=TRUE}
df[complete.cases(df), "id"]        # rows without any NA
```
:::

## Adding rows: `rbind()`

The new rows need the same number of columns and the **same column names**

```{r, echo=TRUE}
new <- data.frame(id = "P6", group = "ctrl", age = 25,
                  score = 21, passed = FALSE, level = "low")
new
```

## Adding rows: the result

```{r, echo=TRUE}
df2 <- rbind(df, new)
df2
```

::: fragment
```{r, echo=TRUE}
nrow(df2)
```
:::

## Adding columns: `merge()`

Add the columns of another dataframe, matching the rows by a **key** (here `id`)

```{r, echo=TRUE}
sleep <- data.frame(id = c("P3", "P1", "P6", "P2", "P5", "P4"),
                    hours = c(8, 7, 6, 6, 9, 7))
sleep
```

## `merge()`: the result

Each row of `df2` gets the `hours` of **its own** `id`, even if the order is different

```{r, echo=TRUE}
df3 <- merge(df2, sleep, by = "id")
df3
```

## `merge()` when some ids are missing

Here `sleep2` has only some of the ids of `df2`, and one more (`P7`)

```{r, echo=TRUE}
sleep2 <- data.frame(id = c("P1", "P2", "P7"),
                     hours = c(7, 6, 8))
sleep2
```

::: fragment
```{r, echo=TRUE}
# only the ids in both dataframes
df4 <- merge(df2, sleep2, by = "id")
df4
```
:::

## Keeping all the rows: `all.x = TRUE`

The rows of `df2` without a match get `NA`

```{r, echo=TRUE}
df5 <- merge(df2, sleep2, by = "id", all.x = TRUE)
df5
```

# Before the exam

## Remember

::: incremental
-   **`<-`** creates objects, **`==`** compares
-   text always goes **in quotes**: `"hello"`, `"5"`
-   with missing values: `mean(x, na.rm = TRUE)`
-   vectors and matrices hold **one type** of data
-   before renaming levels, look at **`levels(x)`**; to reorder and rename use `factor(x, levels, labels)`
-   to use a new value in a factor, **add its level** first
-   lists: **`[[ ]]`** or **`$`** to get an element
-   dataframes: **`df[rows, columns]`**, e.g. `df[df$score > 20, ]`
-   `rbind()`: **same column names**; `merge()`: a **common key**
:::

## Function summary {.smaller}

| structure | dimensions | types | create | index |
|----|----|----|----|----|
| vector | 1 | one | `c()`, `seq()`, `rep()` | `x[i]` |
| factor | 1 | categories | `factor()` | `x[i]`, `levels()` |
| list | 1 (nested) | any | `list()` | `x[i]`, `x[[i]]`, `x$name` |
| matrix | 2 | one | `matrix()`, `cbind()` | `x[row, col]` |
| dataframe | 2 | one per column | `data.frame()` | `x$col`, `x[row, col]` |
